newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New Dutch courier franchise to start in 1997.
newsitem.headline: New Dutch courier franchise to start in 1997.

text.p: A new Dutch national courier franchise, DeNationaleKoerier (DNK), is being launched by three former DHL managers, DNK's general manager Gerdwin Lammers told Reuters on Wednesday.
The new company will be operational from January 1 next year and aims to offer shippers an improved, more reliable service, he said in a telephone interview.
DNK has agreed with around 200 independent Dutch courier companies to market their services nationally using a toll free number.
The service will cost shippers an annual subscription fee equivalent to US$8,000, for which they will get a guaranteed, 24-hour a day courier service, Lammers said.
The new company's manager logistics is John Van Schaik, Lammers added.
Industry sources said Schaik resigned as general manager of DHL Netherlands BV 1-1/2 years ago to create a transport and logistics consultancy group called Quality Consult.
The third former DHL manager is DNK's manager legal, quality assurance and administration, Pieter Bolderhei, Lammers added.
Lammers said the franchise system was designed to avoid uncertainties in the domestic courier market caused by the high number of companies which failed every year.
He said that there were some 2,000 courier companies throughout the Netherlands and although some 500 new ones were established each year, around the same number also closed down.
In time DNK would set up distribution centres in the north and south of the Netherlands. It could eventually expand into Europe carrying packages by road and air, he added.
